gfxStridedData.note: MM2's own mirror of the DirectX 7 D3DDRAWPRIMITIVESTRIDEDDATA, truncated to TWO texture-coordinate sets rather than the SDK's D3DDP_MAXTEXCOORD of 8. Six D3DDP_PTRSTRIDE pairs = 0x30. See docs/gfx_layouts.md section 10 for the two independent stack frames that prove the size and the field order.

verified_unchanged._note: already correct in data/layouts.json. Re-derived here from raw disassembly so nobody 'corrects' them later. No merge is needed or wanted; merge_layouts.py rule 1 would refuse them anyway.

evidence: gfxPipeline::CreateVertexBuffer (0x004AB830) spells the size as a literal TWICE: 'push 0x10; call 0x577360' at 0x004AB8DD and again at 0x004AB904, each immediately before the ctor at 0x004AB660. The previous round reported no literal allocation site; there are two.
ctor(uint count, uint fvf) at 0x004AB690 writes [this+0x00], [+0x04], word [+0x08], word [+0x0A], [+0x0C] and stops - the two 16-bit stores pin VertCount at 0x08 and m_ElementSize at 0x0A exactly
no instruction anywhere in the class or in gfxPipeline's ten VB functions touches offset 0x10 or beyond
gfxVertexBuffer.name_evidence: the binary's .data preserves four verbatim source lines naming the fields: 'lpD3DDev->DrawPrimitiveVB((D3DPRIMITIVETYPE)dm,vb->m_VB,startOffset,count,0)' and 'lpD3DDev->DrawPrimitive((D3DPRIMITIVETYPE)dm,vb->m_FVF,(void*)((u32)vb->m_Verts + vb->m_ElementSize * startOffset),count,0)' (plus the two indexed variants).

gfxRenderState.verdict: the previous round's claim is CONFIRMED; MM2Hook's 0x98 is wrong
independent_evidence: gfxRenderState::Default (0x004B1DA0) does 'mov ecx,[esi+0x4C]' / 'mov [esi+0x4C], 0x006856F0' - it stores the ADDRESS of gfxMaterial::FlatWhite into the object's last dword. gfxRenderStateData already carries 'gfxMaterial* m_Material' at 0x4C in data/layouts.json. 0x4C + 4 = 0x50.

a scan of every absolute dword in .text falling in [0x685690,0x685745) shows dense references to 0x006856A0..0x006856EC (RSTATE's own fields) and then a clean break: nothing in the whole binary references 0x006856F0..0x00685733 except gfxRenderState::Default and the gfxMaterial::Reset thunk at 0x004B1B80. The bytes MM2Hook read as trailing members of RSTATE are a separate global.

gfxRenderState_0x98_refuted.mechanism: gfxRenderState = { gfxRenderStateData State; } where State.m_Material at 0x4C is a gfxMaterial POINTER whose default value is &gfxMaterial::FlatWhite. MM2Hook saw a gfxMaterial-shaped blob immediately after RSTATE and modelled it as an embedded 'gfxMaterial Material' member, giving 0x50 + 0x48 = 0x98. The blob is the separate global FlatWhite that the pointer points at.

gfxMaterial.round2_confirmation: gfxMaterial::Reset at 0x004B1BB0 in raw bytes: 'c7 41 44 ff ff ff ff' = 'mov dword ptr [ecx+0x44], 0xFFFFFFFF', then 'c3'. A dword store at 0x44 means the object is at least 0x48. This is not a Hex-Rays artefact; it is the instruction.
gfxMaterial.second_proof: gfxMaterial::FlatWhite occupies 0x006856F0..0x00685737 - Reset's thunk at 0x004B1B80 sets ecx to 0x006856F0, gfxRenderState::Default writes 0x00685734 (= FlatWhite+0x44), and the next symbol sm_Modelview begins at 0x00685738 (= FlatWhite+0x48).

gfxVertexBuffer_names.change: name-only; offsets and size are unchanged and already correct
gfxVertexBuffer_names.0x00: layouts.json calls this 'Prev'. The ctor does '[this+0] = sm_First; sm_First = this' and the dtor unlinks by walking [p], so it is the forward link of an intrusive singly-linked list. 'Next' would be the accurate name; MM2Hook also says Next for the equivalent link in gfxBitmap.
gfxVertexBuffer_names.0x04: a UNION discriminated by m_FVF at 0x0C. When m_FVF == 0 the object wraps a real D3D vertex buffer and 0x04 is 'IDirect3DVertexBuffer7* m_VB'; when m_FVF != 0 the object is system memory and 0x04 is 'void* m_Verts'. Both names appear verbatim in the binary's source strings.
gfxVertexBuffer_names.0x08: also a union. In the system-memory case it is 'u16 VertCount' (+ m_ElementSize at 0x0A), as the (uint,uint) ctor's 16-bit stores prove. In the D3D-VB case it is a dword: gfxPipeline::PersistVertexBuffer (0x004ABC50) stores a malloc'd backup pointer there, gfxVertexBuffer::RestoreAll (0x004AB730) memcpy's from it, and the dtor frees it. Suggest documenting it as a union rather than renaming.

gfxViewport_names.change: name-only; every offset below is already correct in data/layouts.json
gfxViewport_names.0x120: Flags -> keep. Confirmed as a dirty mask: DoFlush (0x004B18D0) tests bit 0 then bit 1 then stores 0. Bit 0 = viewport rect dirty (leads to SetViewport(&m_Viewport) at +0x15C); bit 1 = projection dirty, set by both Perspective and Ortho ('or ecx,2').
gfxViewport_names.0x124: DefaultAspect -> keep, and it is width/height: SetWindow (0x004B14C0) computes 'fild [w]; fidiv [h]; fstp [ecx+0x124]'.
gfxViewport_names.0x128: field_128 -> a projection-mode flag word. Bit 0 = orthographic: Perspective does 'and al,0xFE', Ortho does 'or al,1', SetWindow tests bit 0 to decide whether to re-run Perspective. The ctor initialises it to 2. MM1's counterpart agiViewParameters ends with 'b32 Orthographic'.
gfxViewport_names.0x12C: field_12C -> Near. Was PROBABLE (MM2Hook's guess); now CONFIRMED. Perspective's 3rd argument lands here ('mov eax,[ebp+0x10]; mov [esi+0x12C],eax') and IsSphereVisible compares the sphere's z against it.
gfxViewport_names.0x130: field_130 -> Far. Was PROBABLE; now CONFIRMED. Perspective's 4th argument lands here; the ctor defaults it to 0x447A0000 = 1000.0f; IsSphereVisible does 'fld [ebp-8]; fsub radius; fcomp [esi+0x130]'.
gfxViewport_names.0x134: field_134 -> TanHalfFovX. Perspective stores tan(Fov*pi/360) * Aspect here.
gfxViewport_names.0x138: field_138 -> TanHalfFovY. Perspective stores tan(Fov*pi/360) here. Because the horizontal extent is the vertical one times Aspect, Fov at 0x174 is the VERTICAL field of view, in degrees.
gfxViewport_names.plane_evidence: IsSphereVisible (0x004B19D0) evaluates exactly four dot products: x*[0x13C] + z*[0x140], x*[0x144] + z*[0x148], y*[0x14C] + z*[0x150], y*[0x154] + z*[0x158], each compared against the radius. The two x-planes are built in Perspective from the aspect-scaled half-angle and the two y-planes from the unscaled one. MM1's agiViewParameters declares 'Vector2 LeftPlane; Vector2 RightPlane; Vector2 TopPlane; Vector2 BottomPlane;' in that same order, consumed by the same SphereVisible algorithm.
gfxViewport_names.plane_caveat: which member of each PAIR is Left vs Right (and Top vs Bottom) rests on MM1's declaration order, not on MM2 evidence. Open1560's own header carries a 'TODO: Are these in the right order?' against Top/Bottom. The grouping into four Vector2 planes is CONFIRMED; the left/right and top/bottom assignment within a pair is PROBABLE.
gfxViewport_names.0x100_to_0x11C: NOT recovered and deliberately left as field_100..field_11C. See docs/gfx_layouts.md section 13.

gfxRenderStateData_field_2C.finding: field_2C, and the 0x2A/0x2B gap before it, are DEAD in the retail binary. No absolute reference to RSTATE+0x2C (0x006856CC) or LASTRSTATE+0x2C (0x006854CC) exists anywhere in .text; no gfxRenderState method touches +0x2A, +0x2B or +0x2C, DoFlush included; and disassembling a 0xC0-byte window around all 131 sites that reference the RSTATE/LASTRSTATE base addresses turns up no genuine hit. No name can be recovered because nothing uses it.

dead_code_findings._note: not layout facts, but they change what the port has to do first. All counts are from an exhaustive E8/E9 relative-call scan plus an absolute-dword scan over the whole image.
dead_code_findings.consequence: every draw in retail MM2 goes through gfxPacket::Draw (0x004B3340 and 0x004B34E0), which calls lpD3DDev's vtable directly. The six gfxPipeline draw entry points and the entire vertex-buffer creation path are dead exported code. Recovering gfxStridedData does not unblock a hot path; gfxPacket does.
